title: If You’re So Smart, Why Aren’t You Happy

questions.q: What is the first of the seven deadly sins of unhappiness?
a: Treating happiness as less important than money or success
Expecting too much recognition from close friends
Spending too much time comparing yourself to others
Avoiding intimacy whenever a relationship gets serious
questions.why: Lesson 1 calls it devaluing happiness: we put it on the back burner and chase proxies instead.

questions.q: What exercise does the summary suggest for identifying what makes you happy?
a: Name the emotions you associate with happiness
List the achievements that earned you praise
Rank your goals by how much money they bring
Compare your mood with that of your friends
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends asking which emotions, such as love or excitement, you connect with happiness.

questions.q: According to the summary, what happens to people who make themselves too available in love?
a: They become less interesting to the other person
They build a stronger sense of trust over time
They attract partners who are equally generous
They avoid the pain of being rejected later
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares it to economics: plenty of supply lowers demand, so constant availability is less appealing.

questions.q: Instead of seeking or avoiding love, what does the book recommend?
a: Being generous, which boosts your self-image and spreads happiness
Being guarded, so you never depend on another person
Being persistent, texting until the other person answers
Being independent, and treating relationships as optional
questions.why: Lesson 2 says helping others shows you can spread happiness from within and improves how you see yourself.

questions.q: What does the dispassionate pursuit of passion mean?
a: Care deeply about your life but view events objectively
Give up your goals whenever they cause frustration
Pursue only the passions that come easily to you
Stay detached from everything so nothing can hurt you
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests staying passionate yet objective and non-judgmental, so you remain patient and flexible.
